title: Overzealous Layer Isolation (DTO to DTO to DTO Mappers)
pattern: Creating distinct, structural models for every single layer of an application, requiring three or four layers of identical mapping code for simple data-passing.
why_bad: It produces immense boilerplate and performance overhead. Adding a single field requires modifying signatures and copying fields across four distinct files, turning basic updates into an exhausting and error-prone chore with zero isolation benefits.
detection: A pipeline where data is converted sequentially across 3+ structs with identical fields inside the same process boundary.
counterexample: Systems where different layers require genuinely distinct representations (e.g., a database model containing rich relational joins vs. an optimized, stripped-down public API payload).
source: Mark Richards, Neal Ford, *Fundamentals of Software Architecture* (2020), Chapter 2; Robert C. Martin, *Clean Architecture* (2017), Part V.
